title: Network Architecture and Models
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 4: Communication and Network Security: Network Architecture and Models.

blocks.text: From Stewart: "The layers are ordered specifically to indicate how information flows through the various levels of communication. Each layer communicates directly with the layer above it as well as the layer below it." From the Official CBK: "The presentation layer ensures that formats are converted and presented to the application layer as needed." Mnemonic (bottom-up): "Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away" (Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application) ⚠️ Exam Trap: Know which layer each protocol and device operates at:

items: Switches operate at Layer 2 (Data Link) — some at Layer 3
Firewalls can operate at Layers 3-7 depending on type

blocks.text: From Stewart: "The OSI Network layer is called the internet layer in TCP/IP and then the bottom two layers of the OSI model are handled by TCP/IP's link layer." The TCP/IP model is the practical model used in real networks, while OSI is the theoretical reference model. The CISSP exam tests both.

items: Encapsulation — Adding headers/trailers as data moves DOWN the layers
De-encapsulation — Removing headers/trailers as data moves UP the layers
Each layer adds its own header with control information
Data at each layer has a specific name (PDU — Protocol Data Unit)

attribution: v2 Unified Edition — Synthesized from 7 CISSP reference books Sources: Destination CISSP (Witcher), ISC2 Study Guide (Chapple), James Stewart, Official CBK (Deane), Shon Harris All-in-One, How To Think Like A Manager (Ahmed) Date: 2026-04-10
cheatsheet: Data Link: MAC addressing, framing, error detection
Physical: Bits on the wire, signaling
Encapsulation: Adding headers/trailers as data moves DOWN the layers
